items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: I started going out to the Palladium and meeting all the bands and writing for them. Red Norvelle and Jimmy Dorsey and all these different bands

ctx.x: California wasn't like New York. My thing -- see, when I first stayed out to California I stayed out there with -- of course, I had gotten an ulcer and stomach and I had to leave Cab's band to stay out there to have medication. And I was offered a job to work in the Club Alabam with Lorenzo Pornoy (PHONETIC). Well, after Cab and them left, that first night in there the delegate, who's name is Elmer Faine, he and I became good friends after that, came

over and wouldn't let me work. So the job only payed $22.50 a week but at that time I had a four room house that I -- with a garage, and rented furnished for $20.00 a month. So anyway, after he wouldn't let me work, said I had to put my card in, I just took my horn home and shined it up nice and put it in the case and put it right under the bed. And I started making -- I had a car and I started going out to the Palladium and meeting all the bands and writing for them. Red Norvelle and Jimmy Dorsey and all these…
Then I finally decided to organize a band and I organized the band and I put the secretary of the union on baritone sax and everything worked out beautiful.
